subject: maths
question: The speed of a boat when travelling downstream is 48 km/h, whereas when travelling upstream it is 32 km/h. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
solution:
**Given:**

Downstream speed = 48 km/h

Upstream speed = 32 km/h

**Concept used:**

Downstream speed = U + V

Upstream speed = U - V

Where, U = speed of a boat in still water, V = speed of the stream

**Calculation:**

Downstream speed = 48 km/h

⇒ U + V = 48

⇒ V = 48 - U ---(1)

Upstream speed = 32 km/h

⇒ U - V = 32 ---(2)

Substituting the value of V in equation (2),

⇒ U - (48 - U) = 32

⇒ U - 48 + U = 32

⇒ 2U = 32 + 48

⇒ U = 80/2 = 40 km/h

**∴ The speed of the boat in still water**** is 40 km/h.**
